---
title: "Why easyNIS: a guide for NIS analysts"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE, comment = "#>",
                      collapse = TRUE, tidy = FALSE)
```

easyNIS turns recurring NIS work into a short, reviewable R workflow: lazily open annual Parquet files, flag code prefixes, build a domain survey design, summarize, and suppress small cells. You keep control of the clinical cohort and analysis choices. Examples use invented data; no licensed records are needed to learn the workflow.

## Before and after: a pooled adult cohort estimate

The hand-rolled version below reads and combines files, filters to adults, then designs the already-filtered data. That ordering drops sampled hospitals with no cohort cases. Pooling also needs year-scoped hospital IDs, annualized weights need an explicit convention, and published cells need a small-cell review.

```{r hand-rolled}
path <- nis_example(years = 2019:2020)
files <- list.files(path, pattern = "[.]parquet$", full.names = TRUE)
all_years <- purrr::map(files, function(file) arrow::open_dataset(file) |>
  dplyr::collect()
) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()
cohort <- all_years |> dplyr::filter(AGE >= 18)
design <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~HOSP_NIS,
  strata = ~NIS_STRATUM,
  weights = ~DISCWT,
  data = cohort, nest = TRUE
)
survey::svytotal(~AGE, design)
```

Filtering before `svydesign()` drops sampled hospitals with no cohort cases. The pooled IDs omit `YEAR`, `DISCWT` is not annualized, and no small-cell check follows the estimate.

```{r easyNIS-equivalent}
path <- nis_example(years = 2019:2020)
nis <- nis_open(path)
design <- nis_design(nis, cohort = AGE >= 18,
                     keep = c(AGE), annualize = TRUE)
survey::svytotal(~AGE, design)
```

`nis_design()` builds the design before applying the cohort domain, scopes hospital and stratum identifiers by year, and makes the weight convention explicit. Its returned design is restricted to the cohort; zero-domain placeholders stay internal for design rebuilding.

## Built-in safety checks

- `nis_design()`: warns “Annualization includes year(s) with incomplete data-quarter coverage”; flags 2015 cohorts with only “ICD-9-coded 2015 discharges (Q1–Q3)” or only Q4; informs when `DQTR` is unavailable for the split check.
- `nis_suppress(hospital_col=)`: masks cells represented at fewer than two hospitals, alongside cells at or below the discharge threshold.
- `nis_cost_provenance()`: records charge and CCR inputs, CPI-U multipliers, base year, and invalid CCR rows; invalid CCR costs are `NA`.
- `nis_prday_completeness()`: counts known, missing, negative/sentinel, and absent procedure-day fields by year and slot.

## One workflow

The same design feeds weighted summaries and models. Suppress the resulting table before sharing it; the function also reports the suppression rule.

```{r workflow}
path <- nis_example(years = 2019:2020)
nis <- nis_open(path) |> nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
design <- nis_design(nis, cohort = AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, LOS, heart_failure), annualize = TRUE)
table_one <- gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(design, by = heart_failure,
  include = c(AGE, LOS)) |> nis_suppress(threshold = 10)
fit <- survey::svyglm(LOS ~ heart_failure + AGE, design = design)
```

Code-era selection is explicit. Slot timing stays matched to its procedure slot; cell counts are year-scoped.

```{r focused-tools}
path <- nis_example(years = 2019:2020)
nis <- nis_open(path)
records <- nis |> dplyr::collect() |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = ifelse(AGE >= 50, "older", "younger"))
toy <- data.frame(I10_PR1 = c("02UG0JZ", "0JH604Z"), PRDAY1 = c(0L, 1L))
charges <- records |> dplyr::select(YEAR, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS)
historical <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2015)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(historical = "428", system = "icd9")
timing <- nis_flag_pr_timing(toy, "02UG0", "0JH60", relation = "after")
counts <- nis_cell_counts(records, by = "group")
costs <- nis_cost(charges, dollars = 2024)
nis_cost_provenance(costs)
```

**What easyNIS does not do / what is still experimental.** It does not replace HCUP documentation, clinical code-set decisions, or study-specific design review. The placeholder-row variance strategy, cost method, ICD-9 support, and AHRQ Elixhauser comorbidity computation are experimental. Suppression reduces disclosure risk but does not rule out every deduction; review derived totals and follow your institution’s DUA process.
